titulo: Determiners: broad range (e.g. all the, most, both)
titulo_es: Advanced quantifiers (each, every, either, neither, both, none of)
descripcion_es: Each and every; both, either and neither for two; none of and all of; agreement with the verb.
resumen: Each and every take the singular; both, either and neither refer to two things or people; none, all and the others take of before a determiner or pronoun (none of the, all of them).

filas: all, seen as a group (3 or more)
Each of the rooms has a balcony.
one or the other / either of the two
You can sit in either chair.
not one (3 or more) / nothing of
None of the guests arrived on time.

explicacion.texto: Neither of / either of / none of + plural: in a formal register the verb is singular (Neither of them is ready); in speech the plural is also heard. With each of and every the verb is always singular.

items: Every never takes of: every one of them, not “every of them”.
Before a pronoun you need of: all of us, both of them, each of you (not “all us”).
Neither is already negative: Neither of us knew (not “didn't know”). With a negative verb you use either: I don't like either of them.
Both … and, either … or, neither … nor: Neither Ana nor Luis came.
Every with expressions of frequency: every two weeks (Spanish “cada dos semanas”).

ejemplos.frase: Each candidate has ten minutes to present their project.
ejemplos.traduccion: Cada candidato tiene diez minutos para presentar su proyecto.

ejemplos.frase: The bus leaves every twenty minutes.
ejemplos.traduccion: El autobús sale cada veinte minutos.

ejemplos.frase: Both restaurants were full, so we had a sandwich.
ejemplos.traduccion: Los dos restaurantes estaban llenos, así que comimos un bocadillo.

ejemplos.frase: You can pay either in cash or by card.
ejemplos.traduccion: Puede pagar en efectivo o con tarjeta.

ejemplos.frase: Neither of my brothers lives in Spain.
ejemplos.traduccion: Ninguno de mis dos hermanos vive en España.

ejemplos.frase: None of the proposals was accepted.
ejemplos.traduccion: No se aceptó ninguna de las propuestas.

errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Every one of the students passed.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Every does not take of; use every one of or each of.
Neither is already negative: do not add another negative.
People is plural; all with a plural takes a plural verb.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with both, either or neither.
ejercicios.frase: ___ of my sisters can drive, so we always take the train.
respuestas: Neither
ejercicios.explicacion: The table's rule for two items applies: neither (of) means “not one of the two”. The clue is the consequence: we always take the train, so neither of them drives. Also, the verb can is affirmative, and the card reminds you that neither is already negative and does not need another negative. That is why Neither of my sisters can drive.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Not one of the two: neither (it is already negative).
ejercicios.traduccion: Ninguna de mis dos hermanas sabe conducir, así que siempre cogemos el tren.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Either
errores_previstos.explicacion: Either means “either one of the two”; to make a negative with either you would need a negative verb (can't), and the sentence has can.

errores_previstos.respuesta: None
errores_previstos.explicacion: None of is used with three or more; if there are two sisters, the correct word is neither.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Both
errores_previstos.explicacion: Both of my sisters can drive would say that both of them drive, the opposite of what the context shows.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with both, either or neither.
ejercicios.frase: I don't mind which film we see. ___ is fine with me.
respuestas: Either
ejercicios.explicacion: The table's rule is either = “one or the other / either of the two”. The clue is I don't mind which film: there are two options and both are fine. Either works as a pronoun here and takes a singular verb (Either is fine).
ejercicios.traduccion: Me da igual qué película veamos. Cualquiera de las dos me parece bien.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Neither
errores_previstos.explicacion: Neither is fine would say that neither is fine, the opposite of I don't mind.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Both
errores_previstos.explicacion: Both would require a plural verb (Both are fine) and means “the two together”, not “either one”.

ejercicios.frase: The doctor checks the patients ___ two hours.
respuestas: every
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule in the list applies: every with expressions of frequency, every + number + period (every two weeks, every twenty minutes). The clue is two hours, which indicates a repeated interval. Each is not used in this frequency structure.
ejercicios.traduccion: El médico revisa a los pacientes cada dos horas.

errores_previstos.respuesta: each
errores_previstos.explicacion: For frequency with a number (Spanish “cada dos horas”) English uses every, not each.

errores_previstos.respuesta: all
errores_previstos.explicacion: All two hours does not exist; all the time does, but for a repeated interval you use every.

ejercicios.frase: Neither Paula ___ her husband wanted to move abroad.
respuestas: nor
ejercicios.explicacion: The card lists the fixed pairs both… and, either… or and neither… nor. As the sentence starts with Neither, the second item is introduced with nor. The verb wanted is affirmative because neither already provides the negative.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ni Paula ni su marido querían irse a vivir al extranjero.

errores_previstos.respuesta: or
errores_previstos.explicacion: Or pairs with either; with neither the correct pair is nor.

errores_previstos.respuesta: and
errores_previstos.explicacion: And pairs with both (Both Paula and her husband), which would have the opposite meaning.

ejercicios.frase: ___ of the three hotels had a free room.
respuestas: None
ejercicios.explicacion: The table distinguishes neither (not one of two) from none of (not one of three or more). The decisive clue is the three hotels: there are three, so only None of works. The verb had is affirmative because none is already negative.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Not one of three or more: none of.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ninguno de los tres hoteles tenía una habitación libre.

por_opcion.None: Correct: none of + plural to make a negative about three or more items.
por_opcion.Neither: Incorrect: neither refers only to two; it does not fit with three hotels.
por_opcion.No: Incorrect: no goes directly before the noun (No hotel had…), but it cannot be followed by of.
por_opcion.Either: Incorrect: either is also limited to two and, besides, it would mean “any”, not “none”.

ejercicios.frase: ___ child in the class received a small gift.
respuestas: Each
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule that each and every take a singular noun applies. The clue is child, in the singular. Each stresses that you are thinking of the children one by one, a natural idea when handing out presents. All would need a plural (all the children) and both is limited to two.
ejercicios.traduccion: Cada niño de la clase recibió un pequeño regalo.

por_opcion.Each: Correct: each + singular noun, each one separately.
por_opcion.All: Incorrect: all goes with a plural or uncountable noun (All the children received…), not with child.
por_opcion.Both: Incorrect: both refers to two and takes a plural (both children).
por_opcion.None: Incorrect: none does not go before a noun; you would need None of the children.

ejercicios.frase: I phoned Ana and Luis, but I couldn't reach ___ of them.
respuestas: either
ejercicios.explicacion: The card states that with a verb that is already negative you use either, not neither, to avoid a double negative. The clue is couldn't, which is already negative, and that there are two people (Ana and Luis). That is why couldn't reach either of them = I did not reach either of the two.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With a negative verb you use either.
ejercicios.traduccion: Llamé a Ana y a Luis, pero no pude localizar a ninguno de los dos.

por_opcion.either: Correct: negative verb + either of = not one of the two.
por_opcion.neither: Incorrect: neither is already negative; with couldn't there would be a double negative.
por_opcion.both: Incorrect in this sense: couldn't reach both of them would mean that I did not reach the two of them together (perhaps I did reach one).
por_opcion.none: Incorrect: none is for three or more and, besides, it would add a second negative to couldn't.

ejercicios.enunciado: Choose the correct option in a formal register.
respuestas: is
ejercicios.explicacion: The card's note on agreement applies: neither of + plural takes a singular verb in a formal register, because the head is neither (not one). The instruction explicitly asks for a formal register, so the answer is is. In speech are is also heard, but in a formal exam the singular is expected.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: In a formal register, neither of + plural takes a singular verb.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ninguna de las dos respuestas es correcta.

por_opcion.is: Correct: in a formal register, neither of + plural agrees in the singular.
por_opcion.are: It is heard in spoken English, but it does not match what the instruction asks for (formal register).
por_opcion.be: Incorrect: be is the base form and cannot work as the conjugated verb of the sentence.

ejercicios.frase: Every of my friends came to the wedding.
respuestas: Every one of my friends came to the wedding.
Each of my friends came to the wedding.
All of my friends came to the wedding.
All my friends came to the wedding.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card's list warns that every never takes of. To keep the idea of “each and every one” you say every one of, each of or, more simply, all (of) my friends. The four accepted answers are correct: they change the nuance (individual with each, overall with all), but not the grammar.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Every is not followed by of.
ejercicios.traduccion: Todos mis amigos vinieron a la boda.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Every of my friends came to the wedding.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: every cannot be followed by of.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Every my friends came to the wedding.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Every does not go with a possessive or a plural; it requires a singular noun without a determiner (every friend).

errores_previstos.respuesta: Everyone of my friends came to the wedding.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Everyone (all people) does not take of; the expression is every one of, in two words.

ejercicios.frase: Neither of us didn't know the answer.
respuestas: Neither of us knew the answer.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule that neither is already negative applies: didn't is not added. The clue is Neither of us at the beginning: the negative is already there, so the verb is affirmative, in the past simple (knew). Spanish does allow a redundant “no”, hence the error.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Incorrect double negative: neither is already negative.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ninguno de los dos sabíamos la respuesta.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Neither of us didn't know the answer.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: double negative, neither and didn't.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Neither of us know the answer.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It removes the negative but changes the tense: the original is in the past and must be knew.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Either of us didn't know the answer.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Either cannot be the subject of a negative verb with this meaning; you say Neither of us knew.

ejercicios.frase: Both of they work in a bank.
respuestas: Both of them work in a bank.
They both work in a bank.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card's list states that before a pronoun you need of, and after a preposition the pronoun is in the object form: them, not they. That is why Both of them work. They both work, with both after the subject, is also correct, as the second answer shows.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: After of comes the object pronoun: both of them.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los dos trabajan en un banco.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Both of they work in a bank.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: after of you cannot use the subject pronoun they.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Both they work in a bank.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Before a pronoun both needs of: both of them; or else they both.

ejercicios.frase: Each of the players have a different number.
respuestas: Each of the players has a different number.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card says that with each of and every the verb is always singular. Although players is plural, the subject is each (each one), so the verb is has. The pull of the nearest plural leads many learners to write have.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Each of + plural takes a singular verb.
ejercicios.traduccion: Cada uno de los jugadores tiene un número distinto.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Each of the players have a different number.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: the head is each and it requires the singular, has.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Each of the player has a different number.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After each of the noun is plural (the players); what is singular is the verb.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence with neither of.
ejercicios.frase: My two cousins don't eat meat.
respuestas: Neither of my cousins eats meat.
Neither of my two cousins eats meat.
Neither of my cousins eat meat.
Neither of my two cousins eat meat.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule of neither of + plural for two people applies, with no other negative in the verb. The clue is My two cousins: there are two. Neither of my cousins replaces don't, and the verb becomes affirmative: eats in a formal register (singular) or eat, which is also accepted because the plural is heard in speech, as the card points out.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Neither of + plural, with no other negative.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ninguno de mis (dos) primos come carne.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Neither of my cousins doesn't eat meat.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Double negative: neither is already negative, so the verb must be affirmative.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Neither my cousins eat meat.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Before a determiner (my) neither needs of: neither of my cousins.

errores_previstos.respuesta: None of my cousins eats meat.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The instruction asks for neither of, and none is used with three or more; here there are two cousins.

respuestas: all of us were tired
ejercicios.explicacion: The card states that before a pronoun you need of: all of us, not all us. The order is all of us as the subject, followed by the verb were and the adjective tired. Another correct form would be We were all tired, but here the words given require all of us.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Before a pronoun you need of: all of us.

errores_previstos.respuesta: us all of were tired
errores_previstos.explicacion: Impossible order: the fixed structure is all of us.

errores_previstos.respuesta: all us of were tired
errores_previstos.explicacion: Of goes between all and the pronoun: all of us.

respuestas: you can come either today or tomorrow
you can either come today or tomorrow
ejercicios.explicacion: The pair either… or from the list applies, to present two alternatives. Either goes before the first alternative (today) and or before the second (tomorrow). The version with either before come is also accepted and is very common, although the more careful version puts either right before the items being contrasted.

errores_previstos.respuesta: you can come today either or tomorrow
errores_previstos.explicacion: Either must go before the first alternative, not between the two.

errores_previstos.respuesta: either you can come today or tomorrow
errores_previstos.explicacion: Either at the beginning would introduce two complete clauses (Either you come today or…); here the second part is only tomorrow, so either goes before today.

descripcion_larga_es: This card covers the quantifiers that distinguish between two and more than two items (both, either, neither as opposed to all, none) and between seeing them as a group or one by one (every as opposed to each). It matters because Spanish uses “ambos”, “ninguno” or “cada” without these distinctions, and because English requires agreement and fixed structures (of before a pronoun, a single negative) that are easy to get wrong.

contexto.que_es: They are determiners and pronouns that indicate how many members of a group are affected by what is said: all (all, every, each), the two (both), one or the other (either), not one of the two (neither) or none (none). Each one imposes its own structure: singular or plural, with or without of, with or without a negative verb.
contexto.por_que_importa: They appear in any precise presentation: comparing two alternatives, talking about all the members of a group or denying that any of them meets a condition. Confusing neither with none, or adding a second negative, produces sentences that a native speaker perceives as clear mistakes, and in a formal register singular agreement with each of or neither of is valued.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: They are used when describing alternatives (either… or), things in common (both… and), total absence (neither… nor, none of) and frequencies (every two weeks). The main clue is the number of items: if there are two, both, either or neither; if there are three or more, all or none. Spanish speakers tend to use a double negative (Neither… didn't) and to say every of, as a calque of Spanish “cada uno de”.
